verses.text: If then you were raised together with Christ, seek the things that are above, where Christ is, seated on the right hand of God.
Set your mind on the things that are above, not on the things that are on the earth.
For you died, and your life is hidden with Christ in God.
When Christ, our life, is revealed, then you will also be revealed with him in glory.
Put to death therefore your members which are on the earth: sexual immorality, uncleanness, depraved passion, evil desire, and covetousness, which is idolatry;
for which things’ sake the wrath of God comes on the children of disobedience.
You also once walked in those, when you lived in them;
but now you also put them all away: anger, wrath, malice, slander, and shameful speaking out of your mouth.
Don’t lie to one another, seeing that you have put off the old man with his doings,
and have put on the new man, who is being renewed in knowledge after the image of his Creator,
where there can’t be Greek and Jew, circumcision and uncircumcision, barbarian, Scythian, bondservant, freeman; but Christ is all, and in all.
Put on therefore, as God’s chosen ones, holy and beloved, a heart of compassion, kindness, lowliness, humility, and perseverance;
bearing with one another, and forgiving each other, if any man has a complaint against any; even as Christ forgave you, so you also do.
Above all these things, walk in love, which is the bond of perfection.
And let the peace of God rule in your hearts, to which also you were called in one body; and be thankful.
Let the word of Christ dwell in you richly; in all wisdom teaching and admonishing one another with psalms, hymns, and spiritual songs, singing with grace in your heart to the Lord.
Whatever you do, in word or in deed, do all in the name of the Lord Jesus, giving thanks to God the Father, through him.
Wives, be in subjection to your husbands, as is fitting in the Lord.
Husbands, love your wives, and don’t be bitter against them.
Children, obey your parents in all things, for this pleases the Lord.
Fathers, don’t provoke your children, so that they won’t be discouraged.
Servants, obey in all things those who are your masters according to the flesh, not just when they are looking, as men pleasers, but in singleness of heart, fearing God.
And whatever you do, work heartily, as for the Lord, and not for men,
knowing that from the Lord you will receive the reward of the inheritance; for you serve the Lord Christ.
But he who does wrong will receive again for the wrong that he has done, and there is no partiality.

footnotes.content: If you've been raised with Christ—and this is the heart of it—then you have a new up. Not just morally up, but cosmically up: where Jesus sits at the Father's right hand. Our seeking follows our citizenship.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The mind settles where we fix it. I've learned this the hard way—when I keep my thoughts pinned on the temporary, I stay anxious and small. Setting your mind on things above isn't escapism; it's reorientation.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: You died, and now your real life is hidden—tucked safe with Christ in God. No one can steal what's hidden there. That death to the old self wasn't an ending; it was the threshold.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: When Christ is revealed—when the curtain lifts and we see Him as He is—we'll be revealed too. Our hiddenness won't be shame then; it will be recognition. We'll shine because we were His all along.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Paul lists the members to put to death: lust, passion, greed. He names them plainly because sin depends on silence. To kill a habit, you must first call it by name and see it for what it is—a rebellion against God who made you.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: God's wrath isn't petulant anger. It's the weight of consequence—the universe closing in on those who turn away from life itself. But notice: this verse points backward to verse 5, not forward into your future if you belong to Christ.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: You walked in them once. Not a confession of shame, but a marker: this is where you were. The past tense matters. You're not trudging that road anymore, and the Lord knows it.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Now put them all away—anger, wrath, malice, slander. These aren't wild passions only; they're the poisons of speech and relation that fester in daily life. The new person in Christ doesn't nurse these grudges.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Don't lie to one another. It seems simple until you notice how much of our social ease depends on small untruths and half-silences. To put off the old man is to stop hiding behind pretense.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The new man is being renewed in knowledge after the image of his Creator—the Creator. This isn't self-improvement; it's restoration, a gradual remembering of what humanity was made to be when God made us in His likeness.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: No Greek, Jew, barbarian, slave, free—Christ erases these lines. Not by denying they exist in the world, but by making them irrelevant inside the body. Where Christ is, the old categories lose their grip.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: God's chosen ones, holy and beloved. That's who you are—not who you're trying to become. So put on compassion, kindness, lowliness, humility. You're dressing in clothes that match your true identity.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Bear with one another, forgive each other, even if there's a real complaint. Christ forgave you—not because you deserved it, but because He chose to absorb the cost. That's the pattern, not the exception.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Love is the bond of perfection—the knot that holds everything together. Not romantic feeling, but covenant choice. Walk in love and you walk in the Lord's own direction.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Let the peace of God rule in your hearts. Peace as an umpire, calling what's true. And you were called to this peace in one body—not in isolation, but woven together. Be thankful for that too.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Let the word of Christ dwell richly. Not a casual visit but a full settling-in, like a beloved guest who makes your home their home. Then teach each other through psalms and hymns and songs—truth rides on music.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Whatever you do, do in the name of the Lord Jesus. The name carries authority and accountability. From small deeds to large, do them as His representative, with thanks to the Father through Him.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Wives, be in subjection to your husbands, as is fitting in the Lord. In its time and ours, this isn't about crushing personhood but about order rooted in love—a mutual surrender that echoes Christ's love for the church.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Husbands, love your wives and don't be bitter. The world teaches men to demand obedience; Christ teaches them to lay down their lives. Love that doesn't sour into resentment is the foundation.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Children, obey your parents in all things, for this pleases the Lord. Obedience here is training ground—learning that there are authorities beyond yourself, and that submission can be an act of worship.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Fathers, don't provoke your children to discouragement. A hard word or constant criticism can crush the spark in a young person. Discipline that comes without love leaves only ashes.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Servants, obey your masters—not just when watched, but in singleness of heart, fearing God. The point isn't to romanticize servitude but to show that faithful labor done before God's eye has dignity no earthly rank can touch.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Work heartily, as for the Lord, not for men. I've known people who pour their souls into work they think is worthless. The secret is to work for an Audience of One, and suddenly it matters.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: From the Lord you will receive the reward of the inheritance. He sees what men don't pay for, what the world forgets. You serve the Lord Christ, and His gratitude is the only wage that lasts.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: He who does wrong will receive again for the wrong he has done—no partiality. Readers today hear an echo here: the Lord sees all, judges fairly, and there are no shortcuts, no hidden favors. That's terrifying only if you live in wrong.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
